title: Trigger-first large language model-assisted adverse drug reaction surveillance: A pharmacist-supervised retrospective cohort study
summary: Among 7,950 exposure episodes, pharmacists adjudicated 28 ADR-positive; trigger selected 167 candidates and caught all 28. LoRA improved false-positive control significantly; sensitivity increase was nonsignificant, and 2 positives remained model-non-positive.
ai_technology: Qwen3-4B-Instruct assesses structured EHR case records for ADR evidence; a local LoRA model trained on 410 patient-disjoint cases involving other medicines is compared against the base model after prespecified electronic-trigger filtering.
organization: School of Electromechanical Engineering, Guangdong University of Technology, Guangzhou, Guangdong, 510006, China; Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University, Guangzhou, Guangdong, 510120, China

evidence.tested: Among 7,950 exposure episodes, pharmacists adjudicated 28 ADR-positive; trigger selected 167 candidates and caught all 28. LoRA improved false-positive control significantly; sensitivity increase was nonsignificant, and 2 positives remained model-non-positive. Two blinded pharmacists adjudicated the full cohort with third-reviewer resolution; the LLM comparison is paired on 167 trigger-positive cases with exact McNemar testing. Internal single-center evaluation for one preparation; no temporal/external validation, explicitly bounded in interpretation.
evidence.ai_role: Qwen3-4B-Instruct assesses structured EHR case records for ADR evidence; a local LoRA model trained on 410 patient-disjoint cases involving other medicines is compared against the base model after prespecified electronic-trigger filtering.
